facts.fact_text: On 25 March 2003, the applicant and others held the picket in front of the Sverdlovsk Regional Court.
On 20 March 2003, the head of the Yekaterinburg public security police ordered that the police should maintain public order and traffic safety during the picket.

On 17 April 2003, an official of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department of Yekaterinburg compiled a report on administrative offences committed by the applicant under Article 20.2 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences.
On 21 April 2003, the head of the Verkh-Issetskiy police department forwarded the report on administrative offences and supplementary materials to the Verkh-Issetskiy District Court of Yekaterinburg.

On 19 May 2003, the justice of the peace issued a ruling on an administrative offence (постановление по делу об административном правонарушении) in which she found the applicant guilty on three counts.

Under section 2 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, organisers of an assembly were required to give written notice to the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly.

Under section 3 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, the municipal authority was required to give its response no later than five days before the assembly.

Under section 4 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, assemblies were to be conducted in accordance with the aims listed in the notice and with respect for Soviet laws and public order.

Under section 8 of the Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988, individuals who breached the established procedure for organising and holding assemblies incurred liability under the laws of the USSR and Soviet republics.

Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code on Administrative Offences provides that a breach of the established procedure for organising a demonstration, meeting, procession or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum monthly wage, which was 1,000 to 2,000 Russian roubles at the material time.

Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code on Administrative Offences stipulates that a breach of the established procedure for holding a demonstration, meeting or picket shall be punishable by a fine of ten to twenty times the minimum wage for organisers, or five to ten times the minimum wage for participants.
